에스겔-6-1.title: 에스겔 6장 1절 역사문법적 주해
에스겔-6-1.exegesis: 17. beasts-- perhaps meaning destructive conquerors ( Da 7:4 ). Rather, literal "beasts," which infest desolated regions such as Judea was to become (compare Eze 34:28 ; Ex 23:29 ; De 32:24 ; 2Ki 17:25 ). The same threat is repeated in manifold forms to awaken the careless. sword-- civil war.

에스겔-6-3.title: 에스겔 6장 3절 역사문법적 주해
에스겔-6-3.exegesis: CHAPTER 6 Eze 6:1-14 . Continuation of the Same Subject. 2. mountains of Israel-- that is, of Palestine in general. The mountains are addressed by personification; implying that the Israelites themselves are incurable and unworthy of any more appeals; so the prophet sent to Jeroboam did not deign to address the king, but addressed the altar ( 1Ki 13:2 ). The mountains are specified as being the scene of Jewish idolatries on "the high places" ( Eze 6:3 ; Le 26:30 ).

에스겔-6-4.exegesis: 3. rivers-- literally, the "channels" of torrents. Rivers were often the scene and objects of idolatrous worship.

에스겔-6-5.title: 에스겔 6장 5절 역사문법적 주해
에스겔-6-5.exegesis: 4. images-- called so from a Hebrew root, "to wax hot," implying the mad ardor of Israel after idolatry [Calvin]. Others translate it, "sun images"; and so in Eze 6:6 (see 2Ki 23:11 ; 2Ch 34:4 ; Is 17:8 , Margin). cast your slain men before your idols-- The foolish objects of their trust in the day of evil should witness their ruin.

에스겔-6-6.title: 에스겔 6장 6절 역사문법적 주해
에스겔-6-6.exegesis: 5. carcasses ... before ... idols-- polluting thus with the dead bones of you, the worshippers, the idols which seemed to you so sacrosanct.
에스겔-6-6.theologicalNote: 5. carcasses ... before ... idols-- polluting thus with the dead bones of you, the worshippers, the idols which seemed to you so sacrosanct.

에스겔-6-7.title: 에스겔 6장 7절 역사문법적 주해
에스겔-6-7.exegesis: 6. your works-- not gods, as you supposed, but the mere work of men's hands ( Is 40:18-20 ).
에스겔-6-7.theologicalNote: 6. your works-- not gods, as you supposed, but the mere work of men's hands ( Is 40:18-20 ).

에스겔-6-8.title: 에스겔 6장 8절 역사문법적 주해
에스겔-6-8.exegesis: 7. ye shall know that I am the Lord-- and not your idols, lords. Ye shall know Me as the all-powerful Punisher of sin.
에스겔-6-8.theologicalNote: 7. ye shall know that I am the Lord-- and not your idols, lords. Ye shall know Me as the all-powerful Punisher of sin.

에스겔-6-9.title: 에스겔 6장 9절 역사문법적 주해
에스겔-6-9.exegesis: 8. Mitigation of the extreme severity of their punishment; still their life shall be a wretched one, and linked with exile ( Eze 5:2 , 12 ; 12:16 ; 14:22 ; Jr 44:28 ).
에스겔-6-9.theologicalNote: 8. Mitigation of the extreme severity of their punishment; still their life shall be a wretched one, and linked with exile ( Eze 5:2 , 12 ; 12:16 ; 14:22 ; Jr 44:28 ).

에스겔-6-10.title: 에스겔 6장 10절 역사문법적 주해
에스겔-6-10.exegesis: 9. they that escape of you shall remember me-- The object of God's chastisements shall at last be effected by working in them true contrition. This partially took place in the complete eradication of idolatry from the Jews ever since the Babylonian captivity. But they have yet to repent of their crowning sin, the crucifixion of Messiah; their full repentance is therefore future, after the ordeal of trials for many centuries, ending with that foretold in Zec 10:9 ; 13:8 , 9 ; 14:1-4 , 11 . "They shall remember me in far countries" ( Eze 7:16 ; De 30:1-8 ). I am broken with their whorish heart-- Fairbairn translates, actively, "I will break" their whorish heart; English Version is better. In their exile they shall remember how long I bore with them, but was at last compelled to punish, after I was "broken" (My long-suffering wearied out) by their desperate ( Nu 15:39 ) spiritual whorishness [Calvin], ( Psa 78:40 ; Is 7:13 ; 43:24 ; 63:10 ). loathe themselves-- ( Le 26:39-45 ; Job 42:6 ). They shall not wait for men to condemn them but shall condemn themselves ( Eze 20:43 ; 36:31 ; Job 42:6 ; 1Co 11:31 ).

에스겔-6-12.title: 에스겔 6장 12절 역사문법적 주해
에스겔-6-12.exegesis: 11. Gesticulations vividly setting before the hearers the greatness of the calamity about to be inflicted. In indignation at the abominations of Israel extend thine hand towards Judea, as if about to "strike," and "stamp," shaking off the dust with thy foot, in token of how God shall "stretch out His hand upon them," and tread them down ( Eze 6:14 ; Eze 21:14 ).

에스겔-6-13.title: 에스겔 6장 13절 역사문법적 주해
에스겔-6-13.exegesis: 12. He that is far off-- namely, from the foe; those who in a distant exile fear no evil. he that remaineth-- he that is left in the city; not carried away into captivity, nor having escaped into the country. Distinct from "he that is near," namely, those outside the city who are within reach of "the sword" of the foe, and so fall by it; not by "famine," as those left in the city.
